To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the G allele of rs560887 is associated with an increased risk of IFGs, and this is likely to be mediated by increased basal hepatic gluconeogenesis.

we show for the first time that the common G allele of the G6PC/ABCB11 gene is associated with elevated fasting glucose levels and increased risk of impaired fasting glucose, and that the association may be related to increased basal hepatic insulin resistance.

the rs560887 G-allele is associated with elevated fasting glucose, elevated fasting insulin, elevated insulin secretion after glucose challenge, increased basal hepatal glucose production and increased risk for IFG.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of the G6PC genes and how these mechanisms contribute to the pathogenesis of insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, and other metabolic diseases.
the genetic basis for type 2 diabetes.
the genetic and environmental determinants of the metabolic syndrome and type 2 diabetes in the Danish population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the G allele in the common rs560 A variant in the glucokinase regulatory protein (GKRP) gene predisposes to type 2 diabetes by increasing hepatic glucose production in humans.
the common G allele in the rs560887 SNP is associated with elevated fasting glucose, increased basal glucose output and increased insulin secretion after oral and i.v glucose loads.
rs560887 is associated with increased basal hepatic insulin resistance, increased fasting glucose and increased risk of impaired fasting glycaemic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rs560887 is associated with increased insulin release and increased hepatic glucose production in response to glucose loads and increased fasting glycaemic concentrations.
the G allele associates with increased fasting plasma glycaemia due to a combination of increased fasting hepatic glucose output, decreased hepatic uptake of glucose and increased insulin secretion.
the common G allele in the ABCC11/G6PC2 locus associates with elevated fasting glycaemia, increased insulin secretion and increased hepatic glucose production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rs560887 is associated with increased basal hepatic insulin resistance.
the common rs560387 G allele in the ABCB11 gene is associated with increased basal hepatic insulin sensitivity and increased fasting plasma glucose levels.
